(2) BF16 trailing fails the 20*n*eps factor gate on n=512 (scaled 32-230); even TF32 fails on band/rowscale/mixed (24-30); BF16x3 matches FP32 accuracy but costs ~3 GEMMs (no speedup). (3) recompute-R-from-Q^TA does NOT rescue low-bit because the reflectors themselves drift. FP32 is the accuracy floor for the trailing. KEY FINDING FOR THE FLEET: the real bottleneck is the PANEL factorization, not the trailing. I tried the fast tensor-core panel alternative CholeskyQR2/3 + Ballard orhr_col Householder reconstruction: ~6x faster on n=512 dense (508->156ms) BUT the reconstruction overflows the factor gate on the ill-conditioned cases (mixed/band/rowscale/rank-deficient) even with an EXACT Q -- orhr_col's unpivoted LU is ill-defined for rank-deficient columns, which rankdef/clustered/nearrank/mixed (5 of 12 benchmark shapes) all contain. This is exactly the well-conditioned-only fast path the task+guards are designed to reject. SUGGESTED NEXT DIRECTIONS: (a) a custom Triton/CUDA FP32 Householder PANEL kernel to beat cuSOLVER's geqr2_smem_domino on the batched tall-skinny (B,m,64) panel -- that is where 73-98% of time sits and it must stay FP32-accurate (workers 0/1 are nearest this); (b) CholeskyQR for the panel WITH a robust per-batch residual-quality fallback to geqrf, accepting that ill-conditioned benchmark shapes (7,9,10,11) revert to ~baseline while the heavy DENSE shapes 3,4 get ~3x -- net maybe 1.5-1.8x if the fallback is cheap, but fragile; (c) leader's ~1300us likely needs a fundamentally different panel (custom kernel), not torch ops.

PROGRESSION: (0) recovered W1's tail REGRESSION -- their cuSOLVER-panel+tf32x3-Triton-trailing path was SLOWER than plain geqrf on tiny batch (n=2048 94k->74.9k, n=4096 133k->50.5k); (1) cuSOLVER panel + torch-TF32 (cuBLAS) tensor-core trailing beats geqrf's SIMT trailing (n=2048 6%, n=4096 4%, geomean 11260); (2) THE BIG WIN: CholeskyQR + Ballard orhr_col Householder reconstruction panel for n=2048 -> n=2048 74858->31619 us (2.37x), geomean 10679; (3) 2-pass shifted CholeskyQR -> 10532. KEY TECHNIQUE (n=2048): cuSOLVER's geqr2_smem panel is SIMT and the bottleneck; replace it with CholeskyQR (G=P^TP; R=chol(G); Q=P R^-1, all tensor-core GEMMs) and reconstruct LAPACK compact-H via orhr_col, whose unpivoted LU of (Q-S) is split into a FUSED single-CTA Triton top-block LU (_toplu_kernel) + a multi-CTA cuBLAS bottom triangular solve. Shifted 3->2-pass CholeskyQR + a numerical (non-data-inspecting) geqrf fallback handle ill-conditioned panels; the looser 20*n*eps tolerance at large n keeps reconstruction in-gate (worst ill-cond test n=2048 mixed 5.93/20). WHAT DID NOT WORK for n=4096 (B=2): CholeskyQR loses badly (B=2 starves every per-panel op -> low occupancy; 58-77k vs geqrf 50.5k); 2-level (narrow CholeskyQR sub-panels + wide trailing, even with closed-form T) is ~6x slower for the same reason and has an upper-triangular correctness bug; BF16 trailing is accurate at n=4096 (loose tol) but does not help (n=4096 is panel-bound not trailing-bound). So n=4096 stays cuSOLVER-panel + TF32-trailing (48619, 3.7% over geqrf) -- it is now the single SLOWEST shape. SUGGESTED NEXT: n=4096 needs a faster PANEL for ONE huge matrix; CholeskyQR cannot (occupancy) and a fused multi-CTA Householder panel needs cooperative grid-sync not cleanly available in Triton 3.6. A genuine CUDA kernel with grid.sync(), or processing the 2 matrices' panels with more aggressive within-matrix row-tiling at the GEMM level, is the remaining lever. Also: the CholeskyQR+orhr_col n=2048 path could likely extend to n=1024 (B=60, even better occupancy) to beat W1's current n=1024 -- worth a brief if it does not regress W1.

CONCLUSION: n=4096 is genuinely at the floor with torch/cuSOLVER/Triton/cooperative-CUDA; the combine's path is the best.
